headline: Local Man Claims His 'Feelings' Were Personally Assaulted By A Third-Century Statue’s Lack of Social Etiquette
body:
Rameshwar Singh, 34, filed a formal complaint at the local police station today, alleging that an ancient granite sculpture of a celestial deity located at a local heritage site intentionally caused him 'extreme emotional distress' by failing to acknowledge his greeting.

“I stood there for ten minutes waiting for the deity to make eye contact or at least offer a polite nod,” Singh explained while holding his printed-out grievance form. “Instead, the statue remained stoic, immobile, and frankly, quite cold. It was an blatant attempt to make me feel small in the grand scheme of the universe, and I simply will not stand for such exclusionary behavior in a public space.”

Legal experts are reportedly scrambling to determine whether a 1,700-year-old rock is legally capable of malice, or if it can be compelled to issue a public apology for its lack of conversational initiative. Meanwhile, the groundskeeper at the heritage site has confirmed that the statue has received no other complaints regarding its personality, noting that it usually gets along quite well with the local pigeons.
caption: When a stone statue decides to give you the silent treatment, apparently that’s a crime now. We are truly living in the future of litigation. #IndiaSatire #IndianNews #PublicGrievance (satire)
igHook: Tag someone who would actually file a police report against a piece of furniture for ignoring them.
imagePrompt: A close-up, out-of-focus shot of an ancient stone statue in a public park, with a wooden police barricade tape barely visible in the foreground.

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 12 wins for pivoting away from the repetitive 'suing reflection/clouds' trope found in the rest of the batch. The premise of taking legal action against a statue for a lack of 'social etiquette' is genuinely funny, provides a vivid image, and avoids the robotic, repetitive phrasing found in the other candidates.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article is a clear piece of satire featuring a fictional individual (Rameshwar Singh) and an inanimate, historical object, avoiding any real public figures, protected groups, or defamatory claims.
